subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow explicit `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field instead of raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: GPU support is already implemented, while the remaining host IPC/raw-args request changes sandbox isolation and public config behavior in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
options.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with validation, docs, create-args support, config hashing, security-audit coverage, warnings, and tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Document GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and keep host IPC unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define broader namespace policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers settle one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
recommendation.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with validation, docs, create-args support, config hashing, security-audit coverage, warnings, and tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the sandbox and security-audit surfaces to this team, and the open choice is a sandbox security-boundary decision.
